title: NVIDIA SimReady Assets Enable Robot Pick-and-Place Sims
summary: NVIDIA launches SimReady Assets for robotics simulation on Hugging Face. Build photorealistic pick-and-place training environments with pre-validated 3D models.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- NVIDIA released SimReady Assets on Hugging Face Hub for building photorealistic robot pick-and-place simulations with pre-validated 3D models.
- The asset library integrates with Isaac Sim, providing physics-accurate objects that accelerate robotics training without custom modeling work.
- Developers can now access production-ready simulation environments to train robotic manipulation systems faster and with higher visual fidelity.


NVIDIA has launched SimReady Assets for robot pick-and-place simulation on Hugging Face Hub, giving robotics developers access to a curated library of photorealistic, physics-validated 3D models. The release addresses a persistent bottleneck in robotics training: creating realistic simulation environments without investing weeks in custom asset creation. Developers building manipulation systems can now pull production-ready objects directly into Isaac Sim workflows.


## What SimReady Assets Deliver


The asset library provides pre-validated 3D models optimized for robotic simulation scenarios. Each object includes accurate physics properties, material definitions, and collision geometry. Common pick-and-place training objects like boxes, bottles, tools, and warehouse items ship ready for immediate use in Isaac Sim environments.


Unlike generic 3D model repositories, SimReady Assets undergo validation for simulation fidelity. Materials respond correctly to lighting and sensor systems. Collision meshes match visual geometry to prevent training artifacts. Weight distributions reflect real-world counterparts, ensuring sim-to-real transfer reliability.


## Integration with Isaac Sim


The assets integrate directly with NVIDIA's Isaac Sim platform, the company's robotics simulation environment built on Omniverse. Developers import SimReady objects through standard USD workflows. The integration eliminates manual conversion steps and maintains full compatibility with Isaac Sim's sensor models, including RGB-D cameras and LiDAR systems.


Physics parameters come pre-configured for typical manipulation scenarios. Friction coefficients, restitution values, and mass properties ship with each asset. Teams can override defaults for specialized applications while maintaining baseline accuracy across standard use cases.


## Availability and Access


Officially launched on November 13, 2026, the SimReady Assets library is available through Hugging Face Hub under permissive licensing. The initial release includes several dozen common objects, with NVIDIA planning quarterly expansions based on community requests. Access requires no separate NVIDIA account beyond Hugging Face credentials.


The assets work with Isaac Sim 2026.1 and later versions. Developers using earlier Isaac Sim releases can access the library but may need manual compatibility adjustments for certain material features. NVIDIA provides migration documentation for teams running legacy simulation pipelines.


## Use Cases Beyond Pick-and-Place


While optimized for manipulation training, the assets support broader robotics applications. Bin-picking scenarios, assembly tasks, and warehouse automation simulations all benefit from the validated object library. Research teams have already deployed SimReady Assets for generating synthetic training data at scale.


The library also serves computer vision developers building perception systems. Photorealistic rendering combined with accurate geometry enables dataset generation for object detection, pose estimation, and grasp planning networks. Several academic labs have published benchmark results using SimReady-generated training sets.


## What This Means


NVIDIA's decision to host SimReady Assets on Hugging Face signals a strategic move toward open robotics tooling. By reducing simulation environment setup time from weeks to hours, the company lowers barriers for smaller teams entering robotic manipulation. The release also positions Hugging Face as a central distribution point for robotics development resources, extending its reach beyond traditional machine learning model hosting. Expect faster iteration cycles in sim-to-real robotics research as validated asset libraries eliminate a major infrastructure burden.
